newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks amble to record close again.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks amble to record close again.

text.p: *Stocks amble to another record close, options related trade features as May series expires. Volume 369.00 million, A$942.76 million value, 1,120 stocks traded, 322 steady, 438 up, 360 down.
Australian shares captured light gains by the close on Thursday, collecting yet another record high and record closing level on the way.
The All Ordinaries index climbed 5.4 points to 2,590.6, having touched a record high of 2,591.5, surpassing the previous record high of 2,590.4 reached on Wednesday.
June share price index futures were seven points higher at 2,602, an 11.6 point premium to the underlying index.
The record closing levels belied a day of mixed trade with the focus on second-level stocks and on the May series options expiries, which caused some hiccups among the leaders.
"Our market was slightly on the positive side," said Shaw Stockbroking dealer Jamie Spiteri.

"BHP is probably the significant mover which has kept the market in the positive," he added, noting that the A$18.50 level was a key one in the May series of BHP options, helping generate much of the bellwether's support on the day.
"You've got options expiry with A$18.50 a relevant strike."

May A$18.50 call options were the most active BHP options with 1,508 traded. BHP shares ended 1.1 percent or 21 cents higher at A$18.60. Some switching from rival miner CRA, which lost 30 cents to A$21.50, also boosted the market leader.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about six to five, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade boomed as May series options expired with 62,807 (56,740) traded, but futures trade was only moderate with 5,420 (6,342) June SPI contracts traded.
In other local markets, short Australian bond yields were near to this year's lows as this part of the curve remained attractive following last week's official rate cut.
By 4.55 p.m (0655 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.57 percent, down from Wednesday's 7.63 percent.

A sudden setback for the yen helped the Australian dollar shrug off early softness Thursday, although the currency again failed to clear key resistance. The dollar was pinned at US$0.7635 support for much of the day but won a reprieve when Japanese industrial production data proved far weaker than expected. By 5.10 p.m., the local currency was back at US$0.7656/61.
